newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Lacklustre amid weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Lacklustre amid weak demand.

text.p: The light distillate markets remained lacklustre on Tuesday amid weak regional demand and ample supplies, traders said.
"The reason the market is so thin is because there is no demand," a gasoline trader with a major oil company said.
Gasoline lifting second-half June fob Singapore was actively offered by a European major but buying interest was thin.

Unleaded 97-octane was offered unsuccessfully at $24.60 per barrel while an offer for 92-octane was lowered from $23.50 to $23.30 where the major sold the 50,000-barrel cargo lifting June 18-22 to a Finnish trader.
The trade was lower than Monday's offer at $23.70 and the last reported deal on June 25 at $23.75 for June 15-20 lifting.
Traders said fresh demand has emerged from Saudi Aramco for prompt supplies of 95-octane leaded or unleaded gasoline, but they were still bearish.
"The market is still long, and sellers are going to be aggressive in tomorrow's tenders," a trader said on the buy tenders from Taiwan and India which close June 4.

Demand is also unlikely to emerge as a result of Shell Company of Australia's shutdown of its 74,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU) and platformer No.3 at Geelong from July 12 for around two weeks, traders said.
If there are any shortfalls, they can be easily covered domestically, they said.
Meanwhile on the supply side, China's export refinery in Dalian had up to two 200,000-barrel cargoes of 92-93-octane unleaded cargoes available in June.
Chinese domestic supplies were tight with other refineries not offering due to high demand but the refinery was committed to exporting its supplies.
Traders said offers for the cargo in second-half June were heard on par with Singapore spot quotes, fob Dalian, but thought buying interest would only be at discounts.
Floating prices on a fob basis are assessed at around a 50 cents per barrel discount to Singapore spot quotes.
Naphtha was quiet but still assessed bearish amid weak Asian demand while Mediterranean cargoes are keeping the market long.
June swaps were steady at $21.70/$22.00 per barrel and July at $21.85/$22.10.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
